confidence_notes: I ran one search for the exchange rate and one for food and drink prices. The search found aggregated Naha and Okinawa prices from several sources, including figures attributed to Expatistan, CityCost and Numbeo. Those sources put a cappuccino at about JPY 430-650, an inexpensive meal at about JPY 800-1,600, a mid-range meal for two at about JPY 5,000 and a draught beer at about JPY 270-500. Some figures cover all of Okinawa prefecture, not just Naha, and the sources vary in how up to date they are. I converted yen to US dollars using my own assumption of about JPY 150 per USD; this rate was not taken from a source. The beer anchor is set toward the higher end of the range because a draught beer in a Naha izakaya typically costs JPY 500-600. I did not search directly for cocktail or wine prices. Both are estimated from the local beer price and general knowledge of highball, cocktail and house wine prices in Japanese izakayas and bars, so they are less certain. All four accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates for the July peak beach season. I did not check any booking pages or current listings for them, so they are the least certain anchors.
comparable_city_reasoning: Based on Naha-specific and Okinawa-wide cost-of-living aggregates, compared with Fukuoka and other mid-sized regional Japanese cities. Accommodation is adjusted upward for Okinawa's summer tourist demand.
